messages:
Ben (sales): Heads-up, DeltaHealth POC hitting intermittent SSE disconnects and partial chunks in their Android client. Happens every ~5–10m during long streams. Need a quick swarm to triage.
Olivia (eng): Can you paste the minimal repro and which endpoint variant you hit (hosted vs dedicated)? Also are you using our SDK or raw HTTP?
Ben (sales): Using Redwood Android SDK v1.3.0 and sometimes curl for repro. URL is our hosted streaming endpoint (redwood.ai/delta/poc/stream). Repro with curl: ```curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://redwood.ai/delta/poc/stream?token=REDACTED'``` Client logs show repeated "incomplete event" parse errors.
Wei (devex): Typical suspects: proxy buffering or nginx chopping events mid-TCP packet. Do you have any upstream proxies (CDN, customer infra)?
Ben (sales): DeltaHealth routing goes through their edge + our CloudFront in front of the hosted API. They also mentioned mobile dataplane customers on flaky networks.
Olivia (eng): Two quick asks: 1) Server-side sample of the raw bytes around a disconnect (slice of the stream), 2) any x-* headers from responses when it fails (x-rate-limit-*, x-request-id).
Ben (sales): Pasted sanitized server snippet from Delta logs:
```
> [2026-02-14T15:12:09Z] write: 512 bytes
> [2026-02-14T15:12:09Z] write: 128 bytes
> [2026-02-14T15:12:09Z] client closed connection: broken pipe
> raw stream chunk: "data: {\"msg\": \"partial\"}\n\ndata: {\"msg\": \"trunc"
```
So you can see an event ends mid-utf8 and missing final "\n\n" delimiter.
Sam (solutions): Also check for intermittent 429s? Clients sometimes reconnect aggressively and trigger short-term rate limits which can cause partial deliveries.
Ben (sales): We did see a 429 once around the same time. Headers: x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-rate-limit-reset: 12
Wei (devex): Short-term mitigation server-side: send periodic SSE comments as keepalive (":\n\n") every 15s and explicitly flush the response buffer after each event. Add header X-Accel-Buffering: no and Cache-Control: no-transform so CDNs/proxies don't re-chunk.
Olivia (eng): For customers behind CloudFront, set origin header to disable response buffering and enable chunked transfer. If using nginx as reverse proxy, set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` and make sure `proxy_set_header Connection '';` so we don't accidentally upgrade.
Ben (sales): Delta team also shared a curl dump showing CloudFront injecting small buffered chunks. They ran into UTF-8 decode errors in their Android parser when event boundary split a multibyte char.
Wei (devex): Client-side fallback: buffer until you detect two consecutive newlines and only then parse an event. Also decode with replacement fallback for partial utf8, e.g., in Java use CharsetDecoder with CodingErrorAction.REPLACE. Quick pseudo:
```
buffer.append(chunk)
if buffer.contains("\n\n") processEvents()
```
Olivia (eng): Long-term: recommend moving POC to a dedicated ingress pool for DeltaHealth so we avoid CloudFront buffering. For the POC we can enable a short-lived dedicated route (requires infra ops and a billing note). Will follow up with pricing and timeline.
Ben (sales): That would help. Delta team wants to avoid UX regressions during trials. Any ETA on the dedicated ingress spinup?
Olivia (eng): I can ask infra to provision a dedicated route in staging within 24–48h. Need official approval from sales for cost; pinging @finops separately.
deploy-bot: New build 2026.02.14-57 rolled to staging for the streaming service.
Sam (solutions): Also recommend client backoff jitter on reconnects to avoid stampeding which causes cascaded 429s.
Ben (sales): Great, I'll apply the temporary client buffering and ask Delta to accept the keepalive header test. Will update here with traces. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
Olivia (eng): Thanks — once you have a few traces (curl -v and the client raw bytes) drop them here and I'll grab tail logs and open a triage runbook.
Ben (sales): Will do. Tagging Olivia and Wei. :thumbsup:
